e: The United States imposes a 10% tariff on Cambodia, citing the presence of alleged forced labour in the supply chain.
Cambodia files a notice to UNCLOS seeking compulsory conciliation of its maritime border dispute with Thailand.
Six Chinese nationals are sentenced to life imprisonment by the Kampot Provincial Court for the 2025 murder of South Korean national Park Min-ho, who was lured to work in a scam centre in Cambodia.
Opposition leader Kem Sokha is granted a pardon following his conviction and 27-year sentence for treason.
A cargo truck and a truck carrying factory workers collide in Kampong Chhnang province, killing nine people and injuring 44 others.
Thailand revokes a 2001 memorandum of understanding with Cambodia aimed at resolving maritime border disputes.

Taiwanese prosecutors indict 62 people, including Chen Zhi, for their alleged links to the Prince Group, a multinational criminal network that operates scam centers in Cambodia. They also charge 13 companies with offences related to the criminal organization and money laundering.
Seventy-four artefacts looted from Cambodia by British art collector and dealer Douglas Latchford are formally repatriated at the National Museum of Cambodia in Phnom Penh.
Opposition politician Sun Chanthy, who had been imprisoned since 2024 on charges of inciting social disorder, is released after receiving a royal pardon.
The Royal Thai Navy seizes a Cambodian fishing vessel along the maritime boundary between the two countries.
The National Bank orders the liquidation of Prince Bank and suspends its operations after founder Chen Zhi was indicted by the United States for large-scale fraud.
Two soldiers are injured in the explosion of a garbage pile in Preah Vihear province.
Chen Zhi, the founder of Prince Group, is arrested and subsequently extradited to China to face charges of cryptocurrency fraud and human trafficking.
